newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Netanyahu "fed up" with accusations against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu "fed up" with accusations against Israel.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he was "fed up" with accusations that Israeli actions were hurting the chances of peace in the Middle East.

"I'm getting, frankly, fed up with the idea that everything we do is a violation of the (peace) agreement, and everything the Palestinians say is in compliance with the agreement," he told a news conference at the end of a visit to Moscow.

The remarks come during a period of renewed tension between Israel and the Palestinians as well as mounting diplomatic pressure against Israel after Netanyahu approved plans to build Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.
On Tuesday, U.S. officials risked further aggravating its ally Israel by saying that, if invited, they would attend a meeting of envoys called by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
"A few months ago we were accused of burrowing a tunnel under the Al Aksa Mosque -- preposterous fabrication," Netanyahu said, referring to Jerusalem's most sacred mosque.
"It should have been thrown out by the international community, thrown out by the international press. It was given credence, this lie.

"I'm not going to accept this same kind of approach again and again," he said. "If the Palestinians are serious about peace, let them sit down with us. If they are serious about airing their differences, let them sit down with us."
